transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, honestly, my job sent me. I do general maintenance, and lately I just keep forgetting... well, everything. Scheduled callbacks, work orders, even just basic follow-ups I promised people. It’s piled up so much. 

Like last Tuesday, I was supposed to fix this leaky P-trap in unit 3B, and the tenant has this little dog—a Pomeranian, I think? Cutest thing, but it barks at absolutely everything. My sister had a Pomeranian back in the 90s named Buster, and he used to chew straight through the drywall, if you can believe that. We had to patch the hallway baseboards like four times because he'd just go right through the plaster... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. The work orders. Yeah, I completely forgot to go back and finish the sink, and that kind of thing keeps happening. So work basically sent me here to get it sorted out before I lose my shot at moving up to a lead position. I really need that promotion, but my desk is just a mountain of forgotten slips right now.
When you were a kid, did you already have problems with focus or staying organized?

Yeah, honestly... I remember being exactly this way way back in grade school, long before I had all this pressure from work. Like, I think about my fourth-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable. She had this massive terrarium in the back of the classroom with a bearded dragon in it. Spiky little guy, but really docile. I used to get to feed it crickets sometimes. Crickets are so loud, though, aren't they? We actually had a huge cricket infestation in the boiler room of one of our apartment buildings just last month. The tenants on the first floor were going absolutely crazy because they chirp right at that frequency that just drills into your skull when you're trying to sleep. I had to call pest control, but the guy they sent out was like two hours late, and he parked his van right blocking the dumpster, which is a huge violation for the trash pickup... 

Wait, sorry. You asked about when I was a kid. Right. 

But yeah, Mrs. Gable and the rest of my teachers, they always told my parents I was really bright. But I was just constantly misplacing my papers. Like, every single day. I'd miss parts of the directions they gave, and they always had to come by my desk and give me extra reminders just to get me to finish my classwork. So it's definitely been happening since I was little.
Do you often feel restless, like you have a hard time sitting still?

Not really, no. Sitting still isn't really a problem for me. I can actually sit in my work van for hours if I need to. Speaking of the van, I had to take it into the shop on Friday because the AC just completely gave out. It was blowing this hot, musty air, and in this heat, it's just miserable. The mechanic said it was a Freon leak, which is funny because it reminded me of this ancient refrigerator we had to haul out of unit 4A last month. 

The tenant moved out and just unplugged it, but they left a whole bag of tilapia in the freezer. Oh my gosh, the smell when we opened that door. We had to use industrial bleach on the floorboards, and the lady across the hall, Mrs. Higgins, came out into the hallway complaining about the odor. She was wearing this bright pink bathrobe with little flamingos all over it. I mean, who even buys a flamingo bathrobe? It was so bright it practically hurt my eyes, and she had these matching fuzzy slippers... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, being restless. Yeah, no, I don't feel like I have to be moving around or anything like that. I'm fine sitting still.
How often do you drink alcohol?

Alcohol? Oh, hardly ever. I mean, maybe a beer at a barbecue once in a blue moon, but that's really it. I actually went to this huge neighborhood cookout over the Fourth of July weekend. My buddy Dave was hosting it, and he has this massive, custom-built smoker in his backyard. I swear, the thing looks like a small locomotive. He spent, like, fourteen hours smoking this brisket, and he kept talking about the specific type of hickory wood he used. He ordered it special from some farm out in Tennessee, I think. 

He was so proud of it, but honestly, his wife makes this potato salad that completely steals the show. She puts dill in it, which I never thought would work, but it's amazing. She actually gave me the recipe, but I completely lost the index card she wrote it on. I put it in my glove compartment, and then when I went to look for it, all I found were these old toll receipts from when I drove up to see my aunt in upstate New York three years ago. The tolls up there are ridiculous, by the way. You can't even drive ten miles without hitting another plaza...

Wait, sorry. Alcohol. Yeah, no, I don't really drink much at all. None, really.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Depressed? No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes with things, but not depressed. Like yesterday, I was so annoyed because I had to go fix this shattered window in unit 2B. The tenant's kid threw a literal baseball right through the glass. I mean, who lets their kid pitch a hardball inside a living room? 

Anyway, the glass went everywhere, all over this really nice area rug they had. I was trying to sweep it up, but management just ordered these cheap new brooms and the bristles are way too stiff. They just flick the little glass shards around instead of actually sweeping them. I tried telling my supervisor, Carl, that we need the softer nylon ones for indoor jobs, but he barely even looked up from his phone. He's totally obsessed with this online auction site right now. He buys all these vintage metal lunchboxes. The other day he was showing off this old A-Team one he won. It had Mr. T right on the front of it. I don't even know where he keeps them all, because his office is already crammed floor-to-ceiling with old paint cans and spare door hinges... 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about being depressed? Yeah, no, I don't feel sad or down or anything like that. Just regular annoyed sometimes, I guess.
Compared with how you've always been, have your memory and attention gotten noticeably worse recently?

Worse recently? Um, no, I don't think so. It's pretty much just how I've always been, honestly. My memory has always been a little... well, you know. Like last week, I went to the hardware store to pick up some of that specific caulk we use for the bathroom tiles. The almond color, not the bright white, because the bright white just looks terrible against the older tubs. Anyway, I walked into the store, and right by the entrance they had this massive display of those little solar-powered garden lights. 

They were shaped like little frogs, and their eyes lit up. I thought my sister would get a kick out of them because she just redid her whole backyard patio. She put down these really nice flagstones, but she had to hire this guy to level the ground first, and he took forever. He was always showing up late, driving this beat-up old truck that sounded like it was missing a muffler. I swear, the whole neighborhood knew when he was arriving. And he always brought his dog with him, this huge golden retriever that would just sleep right in the middle of the yard while he worked...

Oh, wait, sorry. Memory. Right. No, it hasn't gotten worse lately. It's just always been like this.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a lifelong pattern of prominent inattention and disorganization beginning in grade school and continuing into adulthood, now causing occupational impairment. Symptoms include forgetfulness, losing things, failing to follow through on tasks, missing directions, and marked distractibility during the interview itself. Hyperactivity/restlessness is denied, supporting predominantly inattentive ADHD rather than a hyperactive presentation. No evidence suggests depression, substance-related causes, or recent cognitive decline.
